title: Your first fold
story: Fold {{seq.0}}.fasta with ColabFold and put the results in a folder called {{seq.0}}_af. ColabFold needs a GPU and plenty of memory, so start an interactive job that asks for both. Leave the job when you're done.

lesson.title: Folding in an interactive job
lesson.intro: Two commands: one to get a GPU from Slurm, one to fold.

parts.note: An interactive job with 1 GPU and 32 GB of memory. ColabFold runs AlphaFold2 on the GPU; the memory holds the sequence search and the model.
ColabFold's command for folding one or many sequences.
The input: a FASTA file. Each sequence is named by its header line.
The folder for results. ColabFold makes it if it doesn't exist.

lesson.why: ColabFold first searches for related sequences (an MSA) on the ColabFold server, then runs 5 AlphaFold2 models and ranks them.
lesson.without: Without `--gres=gpu:1` ColabFold warns "no GPU detected" and would take hours on the CPU. Without `--mem`, the job gets the default of 16 GB per GPU: enough for a small protein, but a big complex is killed for running out of memory.

tasks.text: Start an interactive job with 1 GPU and at least 16 GB of memory

hints: Inside the job: `module load colabfold`, then `colabfold_batch {{seq.0}}.fasta {{seq.0}}_af`.
